answer: Every ton leaving a pit needs a mine identification number that MSHA binds to one operator, one surface location and one quarterly employment report. A second operation quoting that number draws a closure order, a civil penalty and a call on the reclamation bond. The bond runs 1,800, the dust sampling 600 and the map filing 400, so N clones burn N x 2,800 and each still needs a surveyed pit, a certified foreman on site and a year of water sampling. A marble bench in the office, a ferrous seam in the wall and a relic of the old drift do not make the number new.
